acceptance: finish-this-task runs validate (output captured) after its branch, override and context checks and before its first write (PR-body snapshot, status -> Complete); on failure it prints validate's own error lines and 'finish-this-task: nothing was changed', exits 1 with no Python traceback, and worktree bytes, the index and HEAD are as before

Before its first bookkeeping write, finish snapshots the worktree bytes (or absence) and index entry of every path it may create, overwrite, move or remove before the bookkeeping commit: the chunk, rolled-up ancestors, registry, roadmap.md, roadmap-context.md, the PR-body file and the work artifacts cleanup removes (reusing finish_bookkeeping_undo's path list and state helpers where they fit)

A non-zero validate, export or digest exit, or an OSError or subprocess.SubprocessError during those commands, the bookkeeping writes, cleanup, staging or the commit, puts every snapshotted path's bytes and index entry back (never restoring from HEAD, so pre-existing staged or unstaged edits survive), prints the failing command or path and 'nothing was committed; fix it and run finish-this-task again', reports a failed restore explicitly, and exits 1 with no traceback

tests/test_finish_config_preflight.py through finish's public entry: the rc4 configuration (require_implementation_review_before_finish false, policy.reviewers_required 1) -> exit 1, message names the fix, registry entry unchanged; injected rows for a later validate refusal, a digest refusal after export rewrote roadmap.md, an OSError on the registry write and a commit refusal; one row starts with distinct staged and unstaged bytes on a bookkeeping path; each row asserts worktree bytes, index blobs and HEAD equal the pre-run state and no 'Traceback' in stderr; existing finish tests pass unchanged

acceptance: kill_group, after verifying the group and before its first signal, reads ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,pgid=,lstart= once (lstart parsed as the rest of the line, compared as start_token compares it) and records every transitive descendant (by parent pid) of the group's members that is outside the group, with its start time

After the group is gone, each recorded descendant still alive with the same start time gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after the grace; a pid authoritatively absent or whose start time differs is gone and never signalled; a survivor, or a failed, timed-out or unparsable descendant inventory or recheck, raises WorkerError naming the pid or the failure (the group itself is still signalled as today), so terminate does not report terminated

tests/test_worker_terminate_descendants.py (POSIX), through public worker terminate / kill_group only: a fake harness whose child calls os.setsid(), writes a ready file and sleeps, terminate run only once that file exists; neither the group nor that grandchild is left alive; a grandchild ignoring SIGTERM is SIGKILLed with an explicit short grace; with patched ps/os.kill seams a changed start time is neither signalled nor a survivor, an unreadable inventory and a same-start survivor each raise WorkerError; spawned processes are killed in finally; existing terminate and orphan tests pass unchanged

docs/orchestration-workers.md 'Processes outside the group' says terminate snapshots descendants before the first signal and also ends those outside the group, but cannot see a process already re-parented before that snapshot; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Fixed. Out of scope: processes already re-parented to init before terminate ran, killing by cwd, Windows, worker interrupt
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +40, tests about +130, docs about +3

evaluate_gate, for a leaf whose newest registration commit reachable from the commit under review has the trailer, adds a problem (gate not passed) when the digest at the policy_source ref differs and no valid acceptance matches: 'review policy changed on <ref> since <ID> was claimed (<commit12>): <one line per change: roster <id> added|removed|roles|family|harness a -> b, substitutions changed, policy.<key> a -> b, require_implementation_review_before_finish a -> b>; a human accepts it with `specy-road review accept-policy <ID>` in a terminal, or re-claims the leaf'. finish-this-task checks the pin before review_required, so turning the review switch off after the claim does not skip review; a registration commit without the trailer is judged as today

`specy-road review accept-policy <ID>` runs only with stdin a TTY (otherwise exit 1, 'a human accepts a review policy change in a terminal; nothing was written'), prints the change lines, asks for the node id typed back, and writes work/reviews/<ID>/POLICY-ACCEPTED.yaml (node_id, pinned_sha256, accepted_sha256, user, at) checked against the new specy_road/schemas/policy-acceptance.schema.json on read; an invalid file is a gate problem, never an acceptance, and a later change needs a new acceptance
